text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000401 bills 99215 far above risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity stratum, including on patients with no or one chronic condition, but documentation is too thin to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern is concerning: the elevated 99215 share holds in every complexity band, not just among sicker patients. A third of 99215s fall on patients with zero or one condition, and the sampled low-complexity 99215s carry symptom-level diagnoses such as R10.9, R21, N39.0 and Z09 (e.g., C0213917, C0214270, C0216257). That pattern is consistent with upcoding rather than a high-acuity panel. Against this, the four documented 99215 claims (e.g., C0214246, C0215063) all showed high MDM with no mismatches, and only one of nine notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed lacked a lab or test line. Records cover under 1% of claims, though, so that documentation cannot be treated as representative. A reviewer should first request charts targeted at the low-complexity 99215 claims (starting with the symptom-only visits listed). They should then check whether those notes support high MDM or look templated or cloned."}
